comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C9. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find these background claims about growth feedback mechanisms well-supported by prior literature and treat them as established knowledge motivating the study.

Partial overlap on claims C10-C12. OpenEval finds these definitional claims supported. Peer reviewers group C10-C12 with C13, C63-C67 and express uncertainty about the preselected topology approach, requesting more detail for reproducibility and noting limitations on generality.

Both address claims C13, C63-C67 regarding computational scope and topology selection. OpenEval finds the approach supported with transparent documentation. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, concerned that focusing on preselected adaptive topologies limits exploration and generality of conclusions.

Overlap on claims C20, C21, C25 regarding failure mode classification. OpenEval supports the systematic classification of ~8.5×10^7 circuits. Peer reviewers also support these categorizations, praising the comprehensiveness and describing the framework as 'highly valuable to the community.'

Partial overlap on claims C26, C27 (failure categories). OpenEval supports the classification scheme. Peer reviewers group these with oscillation claims (C29-C31, C55-C56) and express uncertainty due to lack of semi-analytic validation methods and absence of stochastic analysis.

Minimal overlap on claim C28 (bistability/multistability). OpenEval supports the classification. Peer reviewers accept bistability findings as part of comprehensive failure classification, though they note lack of semi-analytic validation.

Both address oscillation-induced failures (C29-C31). OpenEval finds mechanistic insights supported by computational analysis and bifurcation theory. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, raising concerns about lack of semi-analytic validation and deterministic-only analysis that ignores stochastic effects.

Both address bistability claims C32-C33. OpenEval supports the observational results showing 89% bistability prevalence. Peer reviewers also support these findings as part of the comprehensive failure classification, acknowledging bistability as a primary mechanism despite methodological concerns.

Both address optimal circuit family identification (C35-C37). OpenEval supports the structural features identified through computational analysis. Peer reviewers explicitly praise identification of 'core motifs that ensure robust performance' with no specific critiques of these structural findings.

Both address structural determinants of robustness (C42, C44-C46). OpenEval supports the distinction between NFBL and IFFL requirements. Peer reviewers praise the systematic identification of design features as a key contribution, treating these structural findings as supported.

Perfect agreement on claims C47, C49 regarding topology-burden-oscillation relationships. OpenEval supports the computational analysis connecting circuit topology to failure susceptibility. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the praised comprehensive topology analysis.

Partial overlap on claims C55-C56 (major conclusions about oscillations). OpenEval supports these conclusions. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about oscillation findings due to methodological concerns (lack of semi-analytic validation, deterministic-only analysis).

Partial overlap on claim C57 (topology sensitivity). OpenEval supports this finding demonstrated throughout the analysis. Peer reviewers accept it as part of comprehensive analysis but suggest further elaboration on design implications would strengthen impact.

Both address non-monotonic phenomenon (C58). OpenEval supports the specific finding with acknowledgment of potential underestimation. Peer reviewers accept this finding but request further elaboration on implications for circuit design.

Both address generalization to four-gene circuits (C59). OpenEval expresses uncertainty due to limited detail about the four-gene analysis in main text. Peer reviewers support this generalization, accepting it as contributing to broader applicability of the classification framework.
